question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the following integral. Do not round the answer.

$\frac{2}{25}\int_{15}^{405}\frac{2}{\left(\frac{x}{5}\right)\sqrt{{log}_{3}\left(\frac{x}{5}\right)}}\,\text{d}x=($
{{field-1}}
$)\operatorname{ln}⁡3$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=\frac{\log{\left(\frac{x}{5} \right)}}{\log{\left(3 \right)}}.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x \log{\left(3 \right)}}\,⟹\,\log{\left(3 \right)}\,\text{d}u=\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $15$ | $405$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $1$ | $4$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{25}\int_{15}^{405}\frac{2}{\left(\frac{x}{5}\right)\sqrt{{log}_{3}\left(\frac{x}{5}\right)}}\,\text{d}x \\ & =\frac{4}{25}\int_{15}^{405}\frac{1}{\sqrt{{log}_{3}\left(\frac{x}{5}\right)}}\cdot \frac{1}{\left(\frac{x}{5}\right)}\,\text{d}x \\ & =\frac{4}{5}\int_{1}^{4}\frac{1}{\sqrt{u}}\cdot \operatorname{ln}3\,\text{d}u \\ & =\frac{4 \log{\left(3 \right)}}{5}\int_{1}^{4}{u}^{-1/2}\,\text{d}u \\ & =\frac{2}{5}\cdot\left(2\operatorname{ln}3\cdot (2\sqrt{u})\right)|_{1}^{4} \\ & =\frac{2}{5}\cdot\left(4\operatorname{ln}3(\sqrt{4}-\sqrt{1})\right) \\ & =\frac{2}{5}\cdot\left(4\operatorname{ln}3(2-1)\right) \\ & =\frac{2}{5}\cdot\left((4)\operatorname{ln}3\right)\end{aligned}
$$
